prompt: Somebody outside has a working password for an account, but has not used it yet. Is it an incident, by the lesson's definition?
hint: Violation, or imminent threat of one.

choices.text: Only if a rule fired
choices.why: Rules make alerts; incidents are judged.

choices.text: Yes, it counts
choices.why: Right. Success is not required.

choices.text: Only if data left
choices.why: That changes severity, not whether it is an incident.

choices.text: No, because nothing has happened yet and no system or data has been harmed in any way
choices.why: The definition is measured against policy, not damage.

prompt: Match each word to an example from the week.

pairs.right: one of the 382 rows in siem.db

prompt: Which mistake does the lesson say identification guards against?

choices.text: Treating an incident as an alert, or an alert as an incident
choices.why: Right. One loses the incident; the other wastes a team.

choices.text: Sharing indicators
choices.why: Not this lesson.

choices.text: Writing rules with the wrong level
choices.why: Levels are lesson 6.

choices.text: Using UTC in a report
choices.why: UTC is recommended.

prompt: Why does the exact time of declaring matter for the LGPD?

choices.text: The ANPD fines companies by the minute
choices.why: Not how it works.

choices.text: Deadlines run from knowing
choices.why: Right. Lesson 21 shows the LGPD's.

choices.text: It decides who the incident lead is
choices.why: The plan does that.

choices.text: It has to match the SIEM's clock to the second, or the record of the incident is invalid
choices.why: Precision helps, but invalidity is not the issue.

prompt: What does declaring an incident change about the affected systems?

choices.text: They are switched off at once
choices.why: Containment decides that, lesson 13.

choices.text: They are reinstalled
choices.why: That destroys evidence.

choices.text: Their logs are shared with the sharing group
choices.why: Sharing comes later, if at all.

choices.text: Nothing on them is deleted, rebuilt or rotated away
choices.why: Right. Overwritten evidence is gone.

prompt: The lead is unsure whether Thursday is an incident yet. What does the lesson advise?

choices.text: Wait until the investigation is complete, so the record is accurate from the start
choices.why: The record can be corrected; lost evidence cannot.

choices.text: Declare only if the press finds out
choices.why: That inverts the purpose.

choices.text: Declare: downgrading later costs hours, declaring late costs evidence
choices.why: Right. Declaring should be cheap.

choices.text: Ask the sharing group to decide
choices.why: The plan names who decides.

prompt: Match each impact category to Thursday's value.
Nothing stopped working and nobody noticed. Why is Thursday still serious?

choices.text: A privacy breach
choices.why: Right. Client tax files are personal data.

choices.text: Because it happened at night, when the company has no staff on duty to watch the alerts
choices.why: Time of day is not a severity criterion.

choices.text: Because 57 logins failed
choices.why: Failures alone are background noise.

choices.text: Its functional impact is high
choices.why: Every service kept running.

prompt: What does the kind of an incident decide?
hint: Kind and seriousness decide different things.

choices.text: Who is told and how fast
choices.why: That is seriousness.

choices.text: Which playbook applies
choices.why: Right. Seriousness decides who is told and how fast.

choices.text: How much the insurer pays out to the company once the incident is closed
choices.why: Not what classification is for.

choices.text: The incident's identifier
choices.why: Identifiers are just sequential.

prompt: Why does the lesson draw what is out of scope as carefully as what is in it?

choices.text: To make the diagram symmetrical and easier to read in the report for management
choices.why: The reason is evidence, not layout.

choices.text: Because the law lists them
choices.why: No law lists your hosts.

choices.text: Because out-of-scope systems are rebuilt first
choices.why: Out of scope means not affected.

choices.text: "Out of scope" is a claim that needs evidence too
choices.why: Right. Write down what was checked and how.

prompt: Why does timeline.sql fold the 57 failures into one row?
hint: Six that matter, sixty that do not.

choices.text: So they do not bury the events that matter
choices.why: Right. The count stays; the noise goes.

choices.text: Because SQLite cannot print more than ten rows
choices.why: It prints as many as asked.

choices.text: Because the failures are false positives and should be removed from any record of the incident
choices.why: They are true, and part of the story; they are summarised, not removed.

choices.text: To hide them from management
choices.why: The row says there were 57.

prompt: How should "a key was added between 02:35 and 03:05" appear in the timeline today?

choices.text: Only in the report to the ANPD
choices.why: The timeline is where it belongs, labelled.

choices.text: Labelled as inferred from the 03:05 key login
choices.why: Right. Lesson 17 can turn it into a fact.

choices.text: As a fact, because it is obvious
choices.why: Obvious is not evidence.

choices.text: Not at all, until it is proven
choices.why: Hiding a strong inference loses information.

prompt: Starting from 203.0.113.66, which order of questions closes Thursday's scope fastest?
hint: Each answer feeds the next question.

choices.text: The sharing group's report first
choices.why: Your own data first.

choices.text: Address to accounts, accounts to hosts, hosts to what left
choices.why: Right. Each answer becomes the next input.

choices.text: Every log from the week, read top to bottom, so that nothing outside the obvious path is missed
choices.why: That is browsing; scoping follows the links.

choices.text: Hosts first, then the address, then the accounts
choices.why: The address is what you start with.
